clue.text: Fit youngster has nothing for self-defence

blocks.note: A1 means in first-class condition; setters write the 1 as the letter I
a kid is a child
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A healthy child takes up a martial art to protect themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit youngster' reads as one healthy child, but 'Fit' is A1, as in A1 condition, with the digit spelt as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Aikido is a Japanese martial art built around throws and holds, practised as a means of defending oneself.

clue.text: On building a nest, start to feel secure again

indicators.note: building means constructing something new, so the letters are put together in a fresh arrangement
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: re means on or concerning, as in business letters
taken as written
the opening letter of feel

explanation.surface: A bird building its nest begins to feel safe once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a preposition setting the scene, but it is RE, the 'regarding' of business letters and memos.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten is to make something secure, and the prefix re- adds the sense of doing that again.

clue.text: Stretch over, has a rest

indicators.note: turned over means flipped end to end, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a span is a stretch of time or distance

explanation.surface: Someone stretches out and takes a break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch over' looks like a physical action before a rest, but 'over' signals turning the noun round.
explanation.definitionFit: To nap is to sleep briefly, so a person who naps is taking a short break from activity.

clue.text: Man maybe seduced with no protection from doctor

indicators.note: protection wraps around something, so removing the protective outer layer strips away the surrounding letters

blocks.note: to mislead someone can mean to lead them astray or seduce them
MD is Doctor of Medicine; here its two letters sit on the outside

explanation.surface: A man is seduced after a doctor fails to supply contraception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is not a person but the Isle of Man, the island in the Irish Sea; 'maybe' flags it as an example. MISLED loses the M and D that wrap it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is one example of an island, which is what a single short word for island names.

clue.text: Cancel out Tyneside scandal?

blocks.note: Tyneside is in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
-gate is the suffix tagged onto scandals since Watergate

explanation.surface: A headline-writer's call to quash a scandal in the Newcastle area.
explanation.walkthrough: Tyneside is the Newcastle area of north-east England. Any scandal gets '-gate' added after Watergate, so a Tyneside one is NE-gate.
explanation.definitionFit: To negate is to nullify or make ineffective, which is exactly what cancelling something out does.

clue.text: Blasted creature that might get shot on reflection

indicators.note: a mirror reflection shows things the wrong way round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a rabid mad dog is the sort of animal that gets put down by gunfire

explanation.surface: A cursed animal, thinking it over, ought to be shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blasted' suggests the shooting in the picture, but it is the definition, a mild curse word.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamatory adjectives used as curses to express annoyance, as in 'that blasted car'.

clue.text: Fights over one bill where alcohol's served

indicators.note: lying over something means covering it on both sides, so one piece encloses the rest

blocks.note: wars are large-scale fights
Roman numeral one
neb is an old word for a bird's beak or bill

explanation.surface: Brawls break out over a single tab in places that serve drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like the tab at the bar, but it is a beak, the NEB.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine bars are drinking establishments, places specialising in serving wine and other alcohol.

clue.text: Goes off round India with maiden being selfish

indicators.note: going off means going bad or awry, so the letters are disordered
to go round something is to surround it, so one piece is placed inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
India is I in the NATO alphabet
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A traveller heads off around India with a young woman, thinking only of themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goes off' reads as setting out on a trip; 'off' is the signal to rearrange. M for maiden comes from cricket scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is the habit of putting one's own interests first, which is the state of being self-centred.

clue.text: Kidnap victim, female wearing old clothes, turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning something upwards makes it read from bottom to top
whoever wears a garment is enclosed by it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: rags are worn-out clothing
her is a female pronoun

explanation.surface: A kidnapped woman reappears dressed in tatters.
explanation.walkthrough: The victim sounds human, but Shergar was a champion Derby-winning racehorse stolen in Ireland in 1983 and never found.
explanation.definitionFit: Shergar, owned by the Aga Khan, was famously abducted from a stud farm and held for ransom.

clue.text: Gershwin back in Paris

indicators.note: sitting in something means being contained within its letters
going back means travelling the other way, so read right to left

blocks.note: the middle three letters of the city's name

explanation.surface: The songwriter is back in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: George is the Gershwin most people think of first, but the answer is his brother, the lyricist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira Gershwin wrote the lyrics for many songs composed by his brother George, so the surname points to him.

clue.text: Fly to Sweden, get confused and disappear

blocks.note: S is the international vehicle code for Sweden
a ked is a wingless fly that lives on sheep
to addle is to muddle or become muddled

explanation.surface: Someone flies off to Sweden, gets in a muddle and vanishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as a verb about air travel, but it is the insect, the sheep KED; 'to' puts it after Sweden's S.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is a colloquial word for running off hurriedly, vanishing from the scene.

clue.text: Kind drunkard takes in Loomer finally

indicators.note: to take something in is to absorb it inside, so one piece goes within another
finally points to the closing letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: a sot is a habitual drunk
the closing letter of Loomer

explanation.surface: A benevolent drinker gives shelter to someone named Loomer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like an adjective describing the drunkard, but it is the noun meaning type. Laura Loomer is a US far-right activist, fitting the puzzle's conspiracy theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort and a kind are both nouns meaning a type or category of thing.

clue.text: Made up by performing fleas

indicators.note: performers move about doing tricks, so the letters are put through their paces into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A flea circus act is a fabrication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made up' could mean wearing make-up for the show; here it means invented.
explanation.definitionFit: Something invented rather than true is untrue, a fabrication, so fabricated statements are untrue ones.

clue.text: See 15
Silly birds?

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun; read 'Silly' as silly people

blocks.note: first meaning: crazy or foolish people
second meaning: large diving water birds, also called divers

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as one phrase about foolish birds, perhaps silly women in British slang; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A loon is a foolish or crazy person, and the same word names a North American diving bird.

clue.text: Female figure on horseback acquires a following - patriot?

indicators.note: a rider sits on a mount, so the person comes first and the animal follows in the answer
back means going the opposite way, so read right to left
to acquire something is to take it into one's possession, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: a mother, ma, is a female figure in the family
a nag is an old horse; the attached 'back' is the turnaround signal
taken as written
f. is the abbreviation for following

explanation.surface: A woman riding a horse attracts devotees: a patriot?
explanation.walkthrough: The picture is Lady Godiva; 'on' just places MA before the horse. The question mark marks the definition as an example, and a wry one.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of Trump's 'Make America Great Again' movement would describe themselves as a patriot; the question mark hints at doubt.

clue.text: Question One all for now maybe: who is extremely credulous?

definitions.note: a description of a person; read it as 'one who is extremely credulous'

indicators.note: maybe suggests a possible version rather than the actual one, so the letters can take another order

blocks.note: Q is the standard abbreviation for question
taken as written

explanation.surface: A quiz asks whether a one-all score at the moment marks someone gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One all for now' reads like a half-time score, and the capital O on 'One' hides that it is all fodder. QAnon is a US conspiracy movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the QAnon conspiracy theory believe outlandish claims without evidence, making them notably gullible.

clue.text: Former queen and working mother

blocks.note: QU is an abbreviation for queen
a machine that is on is working
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: An ex-queen who is also a working mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Former queen' reads as a single dethroned royal, but 'Former' is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Quondam is a formal Latin-derived adjective meaning that once was, as in 'a quondam friend'.

clue.text: Top student with papers

blocks.note: L is the learner plate
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: The best pupil arrives with their documents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top student' reads as a star pupil; 'Top' is the definition. L for a learner comes from the L-plate on British learner drivers' cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A lid is the cover fitted on a box, jar or pan, the piece that sits on top.

clue.text: Female companion and drunk carrying on in sleeper

indicators.note: carrying something means holding it within, so one piece goes inside

blocks.note: a WAG is a wife or girlfriend, especially of a footballer
taken as written
lit is slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A girlfriend and a drunk carry on together in a sleeping person's presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying on' looks like a phrase for misbehaving, but 'on' is the piece being carried. WAG is British tabloid shorthand for a footballer's wife or girlfriend.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon-lit is a railway sleeping car on continental European trains, borrowed from French.

clue.text: Child grasps right and wrong

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold tight, so one piece is held inside another

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
R abbreviates right

explanation.surface: A youngster learns the difference between right and wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right and wrong' looks like a moral pair, but 'and' is a link and 'wrong' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a tort is a civil wrong, such as negligence, for which damages can be claimed.

clue.text: Pub in Cheers against online service

blocks.note: ta is informal British for thanks
V for versus
E for electronic, as in e-mail
the Royal Navy is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: The bar in the sitcom Cheers takes on an internet service.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Cheers the American TV sitcom set in a Boston bar, but here it is the British toast meaning thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tavern is an inn or public house, a place where drinks are sold to customers.

clue.text: Thought of euphemism finally: 'pre-loved'

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the closing letter of euphemism
pre-loved is a sales euphemism for second-hand

explanation.surface: A sardonic note on the sales term 'pre-loved' as a euphemism.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is itself an example: 'pre-loved' really is the euphemism dealers use for second-hand goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to ponder or reflect, so mused is the past tense matching thought as a verb.

clue.text: Crazy promotion in two thousand and one

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; read 'Crazy' as a crazy person

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: M is a thousand in Roman numerals
an ad is a promotional advertisement
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A wild marketing campaign launched in the year 2001.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two thousand and one' reads as the year, but it splits into Roman numerals for the thousands and the article meaning one.
explanation.definitionFit: A crazy, used as a noun, is an insane or wildly reckless person, which is a lunatic.

clue.text: Overtake swimmer

blocks.note: first meaning: pass someone, written as two words
second meaning: a small fish

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to pass another swimmer in a race; the two words are separate meanings, the first as a two-word phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To go by is to pass someone, and a goby is a small spiny-finned fish found in coastal waters.

clue.text: Left one capital to go round another

indicators.note: going round something means encircling it, so one piece is wrapped about the rest

blocks.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
L abbreviates left
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned one capital city to tour a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like a verb, departed, but it is L. The definition is just 'another', leaning on 'capital' for its sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Berlin is the capital of Germany, so it is a further capital city alongside Switzerland's.

clue.text: Former presenter, one nominally clever, trapped in channel

indicators.note: something trapped in a place is shut inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: Dave is a British TV channel
Roman numeral one
a clever Dick is a know-all, so Dick is the name attached to clever

explanation.surface: An ex-broadcaster with a reputation for intelligence is stuck in a TV channel.
explanation.walkthrough: David Icke was a BBC sports presenter who became a prominent conspiracy theorist. Dave is a UK comedy TV channel; 'clever Dick' is British for a smart alec.
explanation.definitionFit: Icke worked as a sports broadcaster on BBC television before leaving to promote fringe beliefs.

clue.text: Tea dance (a third one)

indicators.note: keeping one third means cutting away the other two thirds

blocks.note: a Latin ballroom dance whose name repeats one syllable three times
Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A tea dance, with a remark that it is the third one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea dance' reads as one afternoon social event, but 'Tea' is the definition; the dance is the cha-cha-cha cut to a third.
explanation.definitionFit: Chai is the Hindi word for tea, used in English especially for spiced Indian tea made with milk.

clue.text: Lamb Smith cooking doesn't require starter

indicators.note: a starter opens a meal, so going without it drops the opening letter

blocks.note: Delia Smith is a famous British cookery writer and TV cook

explanation.surface: A cook's lamb recipe doesn't need a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' looks like the meat for a recipe, but it is the essayist Charles Lamb, who wrote under the pen name Elia.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb published his Essays of Elia under that pseudonym, so the pen name stands for the writer.

clue.text: Drug agent  - it's very fishy looking back

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: a cran is a measure of fresh herrings, so very fishy indeed

explanation.surface: An undercover drugs officer looks over their shoulder; something seems suspicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fishy' suggests suspicion of the agent, but it is literal: a cran is a herring measure, about 750 fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Narc is American slang for a narcotics officer, a police agent who investigates illegal substances.

clue.text: I think Bari's wrong - it's somewhere else in Italy

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters are rearranged correctly

blocks.note: um is the sound of someone hesitating while thinking
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone corrects a guess at an Italian location: not Bari but another place.
explanation.walkthrough: Bari is a real Italian port, which makes it look like a wrong answer; it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Umbria is a landlocked region of central Italy, a different Italian location from the southern port.

clue.text: How to dispose of rubbish janitor regularly collects from scratch

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter, so alternate ones are kept
to collect something is to gather it in, so one piece ends up inside another

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
the instruction 'bin it'

explanation.surface: A caretaker gathers rubbish from the floor for disposal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From scratch' looks like part of the collecting scene, but it is the definition; the rubbish line is the instruction 'bin it'. Bin is British for rubbish container.
explanation.definitionFit: Ab initio is Latin for from the beginning, the formal equivalent of starting again with nothing.
